KEY FINDING that contradicts the brief's premise: tf32/3xtf32 tensor-core trailing GEMM does NOT help -- the larfb/larft GEMMs are rank-nb (nb=24/32) skinny, memory-bound updates, so tf32 gives ~0 speedup AND breaks the factor residual on mixed/ill-conditioned n=512 batches; 3xtf32 recovers fp32 accuracy but is ~4x SLOWER. fp32 SIMT GEMM is both faster and accurate here. The real win was the BLOCKING itself (torch.geqrf spends ~94% in an unblocked per-matrix domino kernel) + a fast custom panel. Final n=512 profile (torch.profiler): GEMM 44.7% (memory-bound floor, can't improve with tf32), panel 29.6%, H-clone memcpy 9% (necessary -- benchmark reuses the input across timed repeats), V-build+larft elementwise ~17%. Cut the n=512 (4/12 shapes, ~18.7ms) and n=1024 trailing-update DRAM traffic, which is memory-bound because rank-nb<=32 skinny bmms make many passes over A2. Two-level blocking: factor a wide outer block (NB=128 for n=512, 88 for n=1024) in nb<=32 emit-VT inner sub-steps, merge the inner (V,T) into ONE outer compact-WY (V,T) via the incremental block formula T_cross = -T_acc (V_acc^T V_new) T_new, then apply ONE rank-NB fp32 trailing update per outer block instead of NB/nb skinny rank-nb updates. Higher arithmetic intensity + far fewer DRAM passes over the wide trailing matrix. fp32. Per-shape vs brief-1: n=512 18.7->16.8ms (1.11x), n=1024 15.5->12.8ms (1.22x); small-n (176/352) kept on a lean single-level path (no outer-block overhead) so they held at 743/1834us. Brief 3 (optimize panel kernel geqr2_vt) EXHAUSTED. Delivered (a): 8769 us vs baseline 116322 (13.27x), commit c0720394 -- new personal best, 1.1x over my brief-2 (8869). FUSED the larft/Gram into the factor loop: after finalizing reflector v_j, reduce g[a]=v_a.v_j (a<j) single-warp-per-a (race-free) and set T[0:j,j]=-tau_j(T[0:j,0:j]@g), removing the separate G=V^T V pass + the sG buffer. Race-free at B=1280 (compute-sanitizer), exact (H,tau), all gates hold. n=512 16.8->16.4ms, n=1024 12.77->12.68ms. ncu PROFILING (works now -- I found and removed a stale /tmp/bisect.py that was shadowing stdlib and breaking all nsys/ncu runs since brief 0): geqr2_vt is OCCUPANCY-LIMITED at 1 block/SM (Block Limit Shared Mem=1; the 64KB staged m*nb panel caps theoretical occupancy at 16.7%), throughput only ~28%, and the top stall is the CTA barrier (~30%). ===WHAT DIDN'T WORK (brief b/c)===: (b) warp-shuffle tree reduction for the norm -> RACES at B>=640 (det=2.0, compute-sanitizer-confirmed write/read hazard on the cross-warp shared combine); single-warp(warp-0)-norm also flagged a hazard. This cross-warp-shared reduction race on sm_120 has now defeated me in 4 forms across briefs -- single-warp shuffle (the dots, the Gram) is fine, but ANY cross-warp combine via shared races at high block counts. So the tree-norm (~8 syncs/col, the bulk of the barrier stall) CANNOT be safely replaced. (c) the individually removable syncs turn out to be necessary on inspection (e.g. the x0=col[j] read must be barriered from the col[j]=beta write). Register-tiling the panel (to cut the 64KB shared and lift occupancy) has a fundamental blocker: with rows in registers, the dot v_j.col_c needs a CROSS-WARP reduction (each warp holds only 1/nwarps of the rows) -> the same race. Smaller nb for 2-block occupancy was tested and does NOT win (extra panels cost more than the occupancy gain; brief-1 confirmed nb=32/22 optimal). ===NEXT===: the panel (55%/49% of n512/n1024) is the wall, occupancy-bound. Brief 5 (halve panel smem -> 2 blocks/SM) EXHAUSTED. Delivered the occupancy lever, but with a key scoping finding that limits its payoff. Best: 7961 us vs baseline 116322 (14.61x), commit 8421aea8 -- personal best, small +0.3% over my brief-4 (7987). HOW: built a low-shared-memory emit-VT kernel (geqr2_vt_lowsmem) that puts the larft T factor in its GLOBAL Tout buffer and aliases the transient norm/dot/larft scratch into ONE nt-float region -> shared = m*nb + nt only. ncu CONFIRMS this lifts the m=512 panel from 1->2 blocks/SM (theoretical occupancy 16.7%->33.3%), exactly the brief's goal. KEY FINDING: applying it to ALL panels REGRESSED (iter0: 7987->8029) because (a) the global-T access adds cost on every panel, and (b) only n=512's m~512 panels actually benefit -- brief-3's sG removal had ALREADY made most n=512 panels (m<=491) 2-block with T-in-shared, and n=1024/2048 panels are fundamentally too large to EVER fit 2 blocks (the panel alone is 88KB/98KB > the ~50KB 2-block budget, regardless of scratch). So the occupancy lever's reach is just the narrow m in [492,512] window. iter1 fixes this with a HYBRID per-panel dispatch: use the low-smem (2-block) kernel ONLY when T-in-shared is 1-block AND low-smem reaches 2 blocks; else keep the faster T-in-shared kernel. That captures the n=512 m=512 occupancy win WITHOUT the global-T regression on n=1024/2048/small -> 7987->7961 (14.61x). Both kernel paths bit-identical, race-free, all gates pass. Per-shape: n=512 15.3->15.1-15.2ms; n=1024/2048/small unchanged. NET: the brief's premise (smem-bound to 1 block) was largely already resolved by brief-3's sG removal; the residual win is small (0.3%) and confined to n=512's largest panels. To get 2 blocks on n=1024/2048 panels you'd have to NOT stage the full panel (register-tile/tall) -- which needs a cross-warp reduction that races at B>=640 (4x confirmed) -- or use W0's launch-shape lever (off-limits to me). nsys/ncu fully working. Next worker on occupancy should target the n=1024/2048 panels via a non-staged layout + a race-free cross-warp reduction (global-atomics or 2-pass), or fold this hybrid into a combine.

BREAK THE fp32 PLATEAU (7550us is ~5x off the ~1300us leaderboard frontier, which uses low precision). Build a low-precision tensor-core trailing update for n=512/1024/2048. KEY INSIGHT: orthogonality is structurally free (checker rebuilds Q from your EMITTED fp32 (H,tau)), so only the factor residual via emitted R is at risk. The prior bf16 negative was bf16x1 - ONE LIMB SHORT. Use bf16x2 limbs (split each fp32 into hi+lo bf16, ~16 mantissa bits, error ~1.5e-5 = 25x UNDER the n=512 gate 6.1e-4, data-independent so NO conditioning dispatch). PRECISION MAP: panel factor fp32; V stored fp32 master + bf16x2 copy; tau fp32; T fp32-formed, bf16x2-applied; trailing A2 fp32 in global, convert to bf16x2 ONCE per wide outer step, do the 3 tensor-core GEMMs (hi.hi, hi.lo, lo.hi) with FP32 ACCUMULATE; emitted R (triu) ALWAYS fp32 written from fp32-accumulated A2. The 4-5x needs low-precision AND WIDE BLOCKS together: nb=128 (recursive 2x64->2x32 panel, inner reduction width<=32 = one warp to avoid the B>=640 race) makes the trailing GEMM compute-bound so tensor cores dominate. STAGE: (1) bf16x2 trailing at nb=32 FIRST, confirm n=512 mixed passes (cheap accuracy isolation); if it fails go bf16x3 (6 GEMMs, ~fp32); if bf16x3 fails too, log the clean negative (low-precision can't hold the gate). (2) then widen nb + recursive panel for speed. fp32 fallback for off-grid/small n. exact (H,tau), all guards. Target 1300-1700us.

Brief 6 (bf16x2 low-precision trailing to break the fp32 plateau) EXHAUSTED -- CLEAN, COMPLETE NEGATIVE on this hardware. No commit; submission stays at my proven fp32 best (7961us, parent 8421aea8) -- the explored bf16x2 trailing REGRESSES, so I did not ship it. THE ACCURACY THESIS IS CONFIRMED (valuable): bf16x2 limbs (split fp32 -> hi+lo bf16, do 3 GEMMs hi.hi+hi.lo+lo.hi with FP32 ACCUMULATE) gives relerr ~9e-6 (vs bf16x1 ~3e-3) and HOLDS the factor gate with huge margin on every hard case via faithful emulation AND a real cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(CUDA_R_16BF in, CUDA_R_32F out, COMPUTE_32F) path: n512 mixed factor=0.24 (gate 20), rankdef 0.15, clustered 0.12, n1024 nearrank 0.078, mixed 0.13 -- data-independent, invariance-safe, orthogonality structurally free (Q rebuilt from emitted fp32 H,tau). The prior bf16x1 negative was indeed one-limb-short; bf16x2 fixes accuracy. THE SPEED THESIS FAILS on this RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120): bf16 tensor cores are only ~1.8-2.6x faster than fp32 on the BATCHED trailing shapes (they hit the 5x ceiling ONLY on a single compute-bound 4096^3, measured 5.0x; the batched B=640 trailing is memory-bound-ish). So bf16x2's 3 GEMMs-per-logical (6 total for the W=V^T A2; A2-=V W pair) cost MORE than the 2 fp32 GEMMs: pure-GEMM best-case (splits precomputed) is 0.71-0.77x for n=512/1024, only 1.07x for n=2048 NB=256. End-to-end (with the per-step bf16 split of V and A2) it was 0.38-0.47x (2.6x SLOWER). Since the trailing is only ~32% of total AND it goes break-even-to-slower, there is NO net win; bf16x3 (6 GEMMs/logical) is strictly worse. ROOT CAUSE of the 5x gap to the leaderboard (mxfp10, 1300us): it cannot come from a low-precision TRAILING alone (only 32%, and bf16 isn't fast enough here). It must come from the PANEL (55%, currently fp32). CRITICAL UNLOCK I verified along the way: Householder Q is EXACTLY orthogonal regardless of the v's precision (product of reflectors), so the orthogonality gate holds even with a LOW-PRECISION PANEL -- only the factor residual (R=triu(emitted H)) constrains panel precision. A future brief should try a bf16x2 (or fp16x2, 10-bit mantissa -> even better) PANEL factorization: that's where the 55% lives and where the 5x must come from. cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx bf16->fp32 is wired and uses the default stream (leaderboard-safe). fp16 was 3.7-4x at 4096^3 (vs bf16 5x) but has range limits for the lo-limb split. nsys/ncu working.
